## Automated Status Summary
#### Scope
The work environment's document library has **no stable document identifiers**. The filename is the de facto identifier, supersession is an ad hoc numeric-prefix convention, and one existing tool there already had to derive a content-hash identifier for recognized text because a path-based key silently orphaned its data whenever a document was renamed. Every downstream capability in this repo (extraction cache, lineage, comparison, evidence pointers) needs an identity that survives a rename and a re-supply.

Evidence: sections C9 and C10 of the work-environment response (https://github.com/stranske/Ready/blob/main/research-program/artifacts/work-bundle/INFORMATION-REQUEST-RESPONSE.md) and the scope section of this repo's README.

#### Tasks
- [x] Add `src/doc_lineage/identity.py` computing a document identity from content: `sha256` of the raw bytes, a `doc_key` of `{entity_slug}/{category}/{as_of}` parsed from path and filename, and a `stable_id` that prefers the content hash.
- [x] Parse the numeric-filename-prefix supersession convention into an explicit `supersedes` field and record `supersession_evidence` naming which convention matched.
- [x] Add `src/doc_lineage/manifest.py` writing `manifest.jsonl`, one row per document: `stable_id, sha256, path, entity_slug, category, as_of, received_at, bytes, mime, supersedes, text_layer` where `text_layer` is tri-state `present | absent | unknown`.
- [x] Make manifest generation idempotent and incremental: an unchanged tree rewrites no rows, and a renamed file keeps its `stable_id` while its `path` updates.
- [x] Add `scripts/build_manifest.py` as the operator entry point taking a root directory and an output path, with no network access.
- [x] Commit a synthetic fixture tree covering at least three managers, two categories, one renamed document and one superseded document.

#### Acceptance criteria
- [x] Renaming a fixture document changes its `path` and leaves its `stable_id` and `sha256` unchanged.
- [x] A byte-identical copy at a second path resolves to the same `stable_id`, and the manifest records both paths without duplicating the identity.
- [x] A numerically prefixed re-supply records `supersedes` pointing at the prior `stable_id`, with the matched convention named in `supersession_evidence`.
- [x] `text_layer` is `unknown` rather than `present` when no check has run, so a later coverage figure cannot count unexamined documents as text-bearing.
- [x] A second run over an unchanged tree produces a byte-identical manifest.

<!-- auto-status-summary:end -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
  - Added document manifest generation for supported library files.
  - Documents now receive stable, content-based identities that remain consistent when files are renamed or duplicated.
  - Manifest entries include document metadata, checksums, and detected supersession relationships.
  - Added a command-line tool for generating manifests from a document-library location.

- **Improvements**
  - Manifest updates preserve unchanged entries byte-for-byte, supporting deterministic and incremental regeneration.
  - Supersession relationships are ordered numerically and scoped to the relevant document path.
  - Documents without recognized text-layer metadata now use an explicit “unknown” value.
  - Invalid manifest output locations are rejected to help prevent accidental library-file conflicts.
